units.text: INT. FAN - CONTINUOUS
It is very good of you, Lord Darlington, allowing Augustus to force our company on you, but I’m afraid I can’t stay long.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Really! I am so sorry! You’ll take a cigar, won’t you?
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Thanks!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Sits down .
To LORD WINDERMERE.
My dear boy, you must not dream of going. I have a great deal to talk to you about, of demmed importance, too.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Sits down with him at L. table .
Oh! We all know what that is! Tuppy can’t talk about anything but Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Well, that is no business of yours, is it, Cecil?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: None! That is why it interests me. My own business always bores me to death. I prefer other people’s.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Have something to drink, you fellows. Cecil, you’ll have a whisky and soda?
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Thanks.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Goes to table with LORD DARLINGTON.
Mrs. Erlynne looked very handsome to-night, didn’t she?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: I am not one of her admirers.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: I usen’t to be, but I am now. Why! she actually made me introduce her to poor dear Aunt Caroline. I believe she is going to lunch there.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: In Purple .
No?
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: She is, really.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Excuse me, you fellows. I’m going away to-morrow. And I have to write a few letters.
units.name: LORD DARLINGTON

units.text: Goes to writing table and sits down .
Clever woman, Mrs. Erlynne.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: Hallo, Dumby! I thought you were asleep.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: I am, I usually am!
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: A very clever woman. Knows perfectly well what a demmed fool I am—knows it as well as I do myself.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: CECIL GRAHAM comes towards him laughing .
Ah, you may laugh, my boy, but it is a great thing to come across a woman who thoroughly understands one.
It is an awfully dangerous thing. They always end by marrying one.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: But I thought, Tuppy, you were never going to see her again! Yes! you told me so yesterday evening at the club. You said you’d heard—
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Whispering to him .
Oh, she’s explained that.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: And the Wiesbaden affair?
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: She’s explained that too.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: And her income, Tuppy? Has she explained that?
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: In a very serious voice .
She’s going to explain that to-morrow.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: CECIL GRAHAM goes back to C. table .
Awfully commercial, women nowadays. Our grandmothers threw their caps over the mills, of course, but, by Jove, their granddaughters only throw their caps over mills that can raise the wind for them.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: You want to make her out a wicked woman. She is not!
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Oh! Wicked women bother one. Good women bore one. That is the only difference between them.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM

units.text: Puffing a cigar .
Mrs. Erlynne has a future before her.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Mrs. Erlynne has a past before her.
units.name: DUMBY

units.text: I prefer women with a past. They’re always so demmed amusing to talk to.
units.name: LORD AUGUSTUS

units.text: Well, you’ll have lots of topics of conversation with her , Tuppy.
units.name: CECIL GRAHAM
